The vocalized form for 'the Lord' here is a genuine book-wide singleton at the byte tier (sweep: 1 book-wide, byte tier: oshb:Job.28.28). A naive skeleton-level search over-collects to 3 hits (oshb:Job.3.19, oshb:Job.28.28, oshb:Job.38.6); of the other two, oshb:Job.38.6's אֲדָנֶ֣יהָ genuinely differs in vocalization (qamats under dalet, segol under nun), but oshb:Job.3.19's מֵאֲדֹנָֽיו shares this word's core vocalization exactly (hataf-patah/holam/qamats) -- it drops out of the byte/accent-stripped counts because it is a different lexeme carrying a third-person pronominal suffix, and mechanically because an intervening meteg breaks the accent-stripped string, not because the vowels differ. A SAMEKH mark follows this verse, and a paseq seg is carried in its single-witness seg layer (oshb:Job.28.28 (setumah, single-witness); oshb:Job.28.28 (paseq, single-witness)). The next verse (web:Job.29.1) reopens with a byte-identical vayosef formula, וַיֹּ֣סֶף אִ֭יּוֹב שְׂאֵ֥ת מְשָׁל֗וֹ וַיֹּאמַֽר (oshb:Job.29.1), matching oshb:Job.27.1 exactly (sweep: 2 book-wide, byte tier) -- so the seam at web:Job.28.28|web:Job.29.1 is bounded by a formula's second occurrence rather than a new one.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding this closing verse into the preceding refrain panel instead of isolating the quotation frame that closes the poem.
literature_type_guess: Fear-of-God colophon closing wisdom poem singleton

boundary_rationale: The vayosef verb reopens Job's voice (וַיֹּ֣סֶף אִ֭יּוֹב שְׂאֵ֥ת מְשָׁל֗וֹ וַיֹּאמַֽר) immediately after the wisdom poem's quotation frame at Job.28.28 (וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָֽאָדָ֗ם...) closes on the fear-of-the-Lord maxim; a Masoretic setumah follows Job.28.28 (oshb:Job.28.28 (setumah, single-witness)), weak corroboration sitting exactly where the new formula begins. The wording matches, byte for byte, Job's earlier resumption formula at Job.27.1 (וַיֹּ֣סֶף אִ֭יּוֹב שְׂאֵ֥ת מְשָׁל֗וֹ וַיֹּאמַֽר), marking this as a second, independent vayosef uptake rather than a continuation of the mashal begun there. The strophe itself opens on a longing formula, “Oh that I were as in the months of old” (web:Job.29.2), built on the one-word wish-verb יִתְּנֵ֥נִי (a mi-plus-suffixed-verb form, distinct from the two-word idiom attested 9 times elsewhere in the book, e.g. מִ֤י יִתֶּן at Job.31.35), and runs through images of divine favor, household intimacy, and agricultural plenty (lamp on the head, God's council over the tent, oil poured from the rock, Job.29.3-Job.29.6) that end at Job.29.6 as the content turns outward to the city gate at Job.29.7. That content turn is the row's stated closing warrant, not a syntactic one: Job.29.3 (בְּהִלּ֣וֹ) and Job.29.6 (בִּרְחֹ֣ץ) are ba-plus-infinitive-construct subordinate clauses depending on the wish of Job.29.2 -- Job.29.5's בְּע֣וֹד is a distinct bet-plus-substantive form on the free-standing adverb, not an infinitive construct, and does not join this pair -- and that same infinitive-construct pattern continues one verse past this row's own edge, at Job.29.7 (בְּצֵ֣אתִי, “when I went out to the city gate”) -- disclosed here rather than adopted as a redrawing, since the chunked span holds the content-scene shift as the seam and finite qatal narration does not in fact resume until Job.29.8 (רָא֣וּנִי, “The young men saw me”), one verse into the row that follows.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival reading folds Job.29.1 into the preceding wisdom-poem span since neither carries a vaya'an frame, but the vayosef verb itself is a distinct formula family and its wording duplicates Job.27.1's rather than Job.28's silence.
literature_type_guess: Job's nostalgic portrait of past prestige esteem

boundary_rationale: A spatial scene shift opens the row's stated content: “when I went out to the city gate, when I prepared my seat in the street.” (web:Job.29.7), moving Job's recollection from the tent and household of the row before it out to the public square. Grammatically, however, Job.29.7's opening בְּצֵ֣אתִי is the same ba-plus-infinitive-construct subordinate form as two that precede it inside the preceding row, Job.29.3 בְּהִלּ֣וֹ and Job.29.6 בִּרְחֹ֣ץ (Job.29.5's בְּע֣וֹד is a distinct bet-plus-substantive form on the free-standing adverb, not an infinitive construct, and does not belong to this chain), all depending on the wish of Job.29.2 -- so the subordinating chain continues across this row's own opening edge rather than breaking there, and the finite qatal narration that actually resumes the main clause (רָא֣וּנִי נְעָרִ֣ים וְנֶחְבָּ֑אוּ, “The young men saw me and hid themselves”) falls one verse later, at Job.29.8. That later seam is disclosed here as the row's own honest rival, not adopted: the chunked edge at Job.29.6|Job.29.7 rests on the content-scene shift to the city gate, which is real, while the syntactic subordination-chain break sits at Job.29.7|Job.29.8. The strophe catalogues the deference shown him there (young men hiding, elders standing, princes restraining speech, nobles' tongues sticking to the roof of the mouth) and then his own conduct as benefactor (deliverer of the poor, father to the needy, breaker of the unrighteous's jaws), holding together as one continuous public-honor tableau through Job.29.17 before a self-referential quotation frame reopens the material at Job.29.18.
strongest_rejected_alternative: One could split the young-men/elders reaction (Job.29.8-Job.29.10) from the ear-and-eye testimony and benefaction catalogue (Job.29.11-Job.29.17) as two rows, but nothing marks a seam between them beyond a shift of grammatical subject within the same scene.
literature_type_guess: Job's justice deeds protecting fatherless and widow

boundary_rationale: A self-referential discourse frame opens the row, וָ֭אֹמַר (וָ֭אֹמַר עִם קִנִּ֣י אֶגְוָ֑ע), “Then I said, ‘I will die in my own house, I will count my days as the sand.” (web:Job.29.18) -- one of 2 verse-initial vav-consecutive-imperfect-1cs tokens of this exact form book-wide (accent-stripped sweep: 2, Job.29.18 and Job.38.11; the two differ in their accents, so not byte-identical to each other), and the only one of the two spoken in Job's own voice as a self-quotation frame (Job.38.11's token sits inside the Job.38.1 YHWH speech-formula span). A wider skeleton-substring search over-collects to 4 by also catching two grammatically distinct forms sharing the same consonants: Job.22.13's perfect 2ms וְֽ֭אָמַרְתָּ (Eliphaz addressing Job, not a self-quotation) and Job.7.4's perfect 1cs וְאָמַ֗רְתִּי (word 3 of its verse, not verse-initial) -- this is the skeleton-is-substring-not-root hazard the toolkit documents. The row turns from the gate-scene catalogue to Job's private expectation of an unbroken future (nest, sand, spread roots, renewed bow). The strophe then returns, without a new formula, to public deference (“Men listened to me, waited, and kept silence for my counsel.” web:Job.29.21) and closes the chapter's reminiscence on the king-in-the-army, comforter-of-mourners simile, “I chose out their way, and sat as chief. I lived as a king in the army, as one who comforts the mourners.” (web:Job.29.25), the row's natural terminus before the adversative that opens Job.30.1.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The private-confidence images of Job.29.18-Job.29.20 could stand as their own short row framed by the quotation verb, but nothing marks a return seam at Job.29.20|Job.29.21 comparable to the frame that opens Job.29.18, so the chapter's closing material is kept whole.
literature_type_guess: Job's hope of enduring blessing like renewed phoenix

boundary_rationale: וְעַתָּ֤ה (וְעַתָּ֤ה שָֽׂחֲק֣וּ עָלַי֮ צְעִירִ֥ים), “But now those who are younger than I have me in derision” (web:Job.30.1), opens the chapter's antithesis to Job.29 with the initial occurrence of three of this 'but now' marker that structure Job's present-misery complaint (sweep: 3 of 8 book-wide tokens of this marker fall in this chapter, at Job.30.1, Job.30.9, Job.30.16). The row describes the outcasts who now mock him -- their degraded origin, gaunt hunger, and expulsion from human company -- as one continuous third-person description that ends at Job.30.8, before the subject shifts to Job's own experience of their scorn at Job.30.9.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading Job.29.25|Job.30.1 as one continuous strophe is possible on parallelism grounds alone, but the adversative particle plus the reversal of content (from honored elder to mocked outcast) marks a genuine participant and register change, not mere texture.
literature_type_guess: Youth's mockery making Job their derision target

boundary_rationale: The second occurrence of the marker, וְ֭עַתָּה נְגִינָתָ֣ם הָיִ֑יתִי ..., “Now I have become their song. Yes, I am a byword to them.” (web:Job.30.9), pivots from describing the outcasts to Job's own degradation at their hands -- become their taunt-song, spat on, their cord loosed against him, an assaulting rabble breaching his path like floodwater -- closing on the wind-and-cloud imagery of Job.30.15 (תִּרְדֹּ֣ף כָּ֭רוּחַ נְדִבָתִ֑י / וּ֝כְעָ֗ב עָבְרָ֥ה יְשֻׁעָתִֽי, “They chase my honor as the wind... My welfare has passed away as a cloud.” web:Job.30.15) before the third occurrence of the marker reopens the complaint as direct address to God.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The mockery catalogue of Job.30.9-Job.30.10 and the assault imagery of Job.30.11-Job.30.15 differ enough in register that a two-row split is defensible; the two halves are not, however, uniform third-party hostility in the same tense throughout: Job.30.11's פִ֭תַּח and וַיְעַנֵּ֑נִי are singular 3ms against שִׁלֵּֽחוּ's 3cp in the same verse (the verse also carries a ketiv/qere note at יתרו/יִתְרִ֣י, neither reading plural), and the span alternates qatal (הָיִ֑יתִי, Job.30.9) against a run of yiqtol forms from Job.30.12 (יָ֫ק֥וּמוּ, יֹעִ֑ילוּ, יֶאֱתָ֑יוּ, תִּרְדֹּ֣ף). Absent any tier-1 marker at Job.30.10|Job.30.11 itself, the row is kept whole under the chapter's threefold marker structure rather than split there.
literature_type_guess: Affliction's terror assaulting like chaos and storm

boundary_rationale: The third occurrence of the marker, וְעַתָּ֗ה עָ֭לַי תִּשְׁתַּפֵּ֣ךְ נַפְשִׁ֑י ..., “Now my soul is poured out within me. Days of affliction have taken hold of me.” (web:Job.30.16), turns the complaint inward. Job.30.16-Job.30.19 run in third-person and 1cs forms (תִּשְׁתַּפֵּ֣ךְ ... יֹ֭אחֲז֣וּנִי, נִקַּ֣ר, יִתְחַפֵּ֣שׂ, הֹרָ֥נִי ... וָ֝אֶתְמַשֵּׁ֗ל), with unambiguous second-person marking beginning just at Job.30.20's אֲשַׁוַּ֣ע אֵ֭לֶיךָ וְלֹ֣א תַעֲנֵ֑נִי (“I cry to you, and you do not answer me.” web:Job.30.20), running through יָדְךָ֣ תִשְׂטְמֵֽנִי (Job.30.21) and תְּשִׁיבֵ֑נִי (Job.30.23). This second-person block from Job.30.20 is bounded on the near side by the marker (which itself opens in 3rd/1cs person) and on the far side by a shift back to impersonal, third-party reflection at Job.30.24.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Some would carry the direct address through to Job.30.31 as one long unit, but the addressee changes from God (Job.30.20-Job.30.23) to an unnamed general subject once the row's material ends, which is reason enough to seam the two apart. The same unambiguous-second-person criterion that supports that far edge argues, with equal or greater force, for a seam at Job.30.19|Job.30.20 rather than treating Job.30.16-Job.30.19 as already part of the second-person block; that internal seam is disclosed as a live rival to the row's own front portion, not adopted, since the chapter's threefold marker keeps Job.30.16 as this row's opening.
literature_type_guess: Job's self-dissolution cry into dust and darkness

boundary_rationale: אַ֣ךְ, “However doesn’t one stretch out a hand in his fall” (web:Job.30.24), turns from direct address to a general maxim about compassion toward the fallen, then to Job's own record of weeping for the needy (Job.30.25), and closes the chapter with a return to self-directed lament -- blackened skin, burning bones, harp and pipe turned to mourning at Job.30.31, “Therefore my harp has turned to mourning, and my pipe into the voice of those who weep.” (web:Job.30.31) -- a cadence that answers, in reverse, the counsel-and-comfort close of Job.29.25.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The opening particle here is weaker than the chapter's three-times-repeated 'but now' marker, so an alternative keeps Job.30.24-Job.30.31 attached to the preceding direct-address block as its closing application rather than a fresh strophe.
literature_type_guess: Job's weeping for afflicted despite own anguish

boundary_rationale: No new speech formula opens Job.31 -- it remains inside the Job.29.1 vayosef span -- but the genre shifts abruptly from lament to legal self-asseveration: בְּ֭רִית כָּרַ֣תִּי לְעֵינָ֑י ..., “I made a covenant with my eyes; how then should I look lustfully at a young woman?” (web:Job.31.1). The row states the covenant with the eyes and its rationale (calamity as God's portion for the wicked) as a four-verse prologue, closing on the rhetorical question “Doesn’t he see my ways, and count all my steps?” (web:Job.31.4), which sets up the opening conditional protasis at Job.31.5.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Job.31.1-Job.31.4 could be folded into the oath that follows (Job.31.5-Job.31.8) as its rationale clause rather than standing alone, but the covenant statement and its grounding question use no conditional particle at all, unlike the chapter's אם particle-token series, which sweeps 17 tokens over 17 verses from Job.31.5 to Job.31.39 (including the oath-affirmation אם לא at Job.31.36, itself not a protasis) -- a series that does not reach every strophe of the chapter, since Job.31.35 opens instead on the two-word wish idiom מִ֤י יִתֶּן with no conditional particle of its own.
literature_type_guess: Eye-covenant opening comprehensive integrity-oath section

boundary_rationale: The oath series proper begins: אִם הָלַ֥כְתִּי עִם שָׁ֑וְא ..., “If I have walked with falsehood, and my foot has hurried to deceit” (web:Job.31.5), the opening member of a 17-token protasis-particle sweep spanning the rest of the chapter, to Job.31.39 (sweep: 17 book-wide-in-ch31). A second clause of the same particle follows at Job.31.7 ('if my step has turned out of the way'), and the pair resolves in one apodosis at Job.31.8 ('then let me sow, and let another eat'). A Masoretic petuchah follows Job.31.7 (oshb:Job.31.7 (petuchah, single-witness)) -- weak, non-driving corroboration that falls inside this protasis-apodosis unit rather than at its edge, and is disclosed without redrawing the row.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The Masoretic petuchah (single-witness) after Job.31.7 might tempt a split before the apodosis at Job.31.8, but marks stay tier-3 corroboration in Writings and do not drive a boundary that would sever a protasis pair from the one apodosis answering both.
literature_type_guess: Oath against adultery's lust and marriage deception

boundary_rationale: A new protasis opens the oath, אִם נִפְתָּ֣ה לִ֭בִּי עַל ..., “If my heart has been enticed to a woman, and I have laid wait at my neighbor’s door” (web:Job.31.9), shifting the subject matter from general deceit to adultery. The apodosis-curse follows immediately at Job.31.10 ('then let my wife grind for another'), and the unit closes with the penalty rationale at Job.31.11-Job.31.12 ('a fire that consumes to destruction'), a self-contained protasis-apodosis-ground sequence distinct in topic from both the preceding and following oaths.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Grouping Job.31.9-Job.31.12 with the falsehood oath immediately before it would produce an eight-verse row, but the topic changes completely at the Job.31.9 protasis and nothing carries over from Job.31.8's apodosis.
literature_type_guess: Oath against mistreatment of servants male and female

boundary_rationale: אִם אֶמְאַ֗ס מִשְׁפַּ֣ט עַ֭בְדִּי ..., “If I have despised the cause of my male servant or of my female servant, when they contended with me” (web:Job.31.13), opens a third oath on the treatment of servants, its apodosis cast as a rhetorical question ('what then will I do when God rises up?', Job.31.14) rather than a curse-formula, and grounded in a shared-creation argument: “Didn’t he who made me in the womb make him? Didn’t one fashion us in the womb?” (web:Job.31.15; הֲֽ֝לֹא בַ֭בֶּטֶן עֹשֵׂ֣נִי עָשָׂ֑הוּ וַ֝יְכֻנֶ֗נּוּ בָּרֶ֥חֶם אֶחָֽד, oshb:Job.31.15). The two womb-nouns of that argument, בטן and רחם, are not this row's own coinage: the final-nun spelling בטן sweeps 6 book-wide at skeleton tier (Job.1.21, Job.3.11, Job.10.19, Job.31.15, Job.31.18, Job.38.29) -- a medial-nun spelling בטנ (suffixed/prefixed forms) adds a further 10 verses book-wide, not needed for this row's own point -- and רחם sweeps 5, complete at skeleton tier (Job.3.11, Job.10.18, Job.24.20, Job.31.15, Job.38.8); a member of בטן -- Job.31.18's וּמִבֶּ֖טֶן -- falls three verses past this row's own close, inside the compassion oath that follows (רחם has no member past this row's own close), so the device the row leans on to set this oath apart is not confined to this row's own span.
strongest_rejected_alternative: At three verses this row ties one other true oath block in the chapter (Job.31.38-Job.31.40, also 3 verses) for the chapter's shortest oath blocks -- the equal-length strophe at Job.31.35-Job.31.37 carries no אם token of its own and is not itself an oath block -- so length alone distinguishes nothing between the two; a reader could attach it to the adultery oath before it or the compassion oath after it, but its protasis is independently marked at Job.31.13, and its apodosis is its own self-contained rhetorical question rather than a curse shared with either neighbor.
literature_type_guess: Oath denying sustenance or shelter to orphan poor

boundary_rationale: The chapter's longest oath opens here, אִם אֶ֭מְנַע מֵחֵ֣פֶץ דַּלִּ֑ים ..., “If I have withheld the poor from their desire, or have caused the eyes of the widow to fail” (web:Job.31.16), and gathers four protasis clauses on compassion for the vulnerable -- Job.31.16, Job.31.19 (אִם אֶרְאֶ֣ה א֭וֹבֵד מִבְּלִ֣י ..., “if I have seen any perish for want of clothing, or that the needy had no covering” web:Job.31.19), Job.31.20 (a further 'if not' clause on warming the needy with fleece), and Job.31.21 (אִם הֲנִיפ֣וֹתִי עַל יָת֣וֹם ..., 'if I have lifted up my hand against the fatherless') -- before one shared apodosis-curse at Job.31.22 (כְּ֭תֵפִי מִשִּׁכְמָ֣ה תִפּ֑וֹל ..., 'then let my shoulder fall from the shoulder blade', web:Job.31.22) and its motive clause at Job.31.23. All four protases fall inside this span, none straddling its edges.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Each of the four protases could in principle open its own row, but they share one topic, one apodosis, and one motive clause, so treating any one of these protasis tokens inside the cluster as a row boundary would cut a syntactically unified oath in pieces.
literature_type_guess: Oath against gold's seduction and wealth-worship idolatry

boundary_rationale: אִם שַׂ֣מְתִּי זָהָ֣ב כִּסְלִ֑י ..., “If I have made gold my hope, and have said to the fine gold, ‘You are my confidence;’” (web:Job.31.24), opens a materialism sequence containing three independently verse-initial protases, not two: trust in gold (Job.31.24), a further wealth-increase clause (Job.31.25, אִם אֶ֭שְׂמַח כִּי רַ֣ב חֵילִ֑י..., “If I have rejoiced because my wealth was great” web:Job.31.25), and astral reverence for sun and moon (Job.31.26, אִם אֶרְאֶ֣ה א֖וֹר כִּ֣י יָהֵ֑ל ...וְ֝יָרֵ֗חַ יָקָ֥ר הֹלֵֽךְ, “if I have seen the sun when it shined, or the moon moving in splendor,” web:Job.31.26). One apodosis follows at Job.31.28 (גַּם ה֭וּא עָוֺ֣ן פְּלִילִ֑י, “this also would be an iniquity to be punished by the judges, for I would have denied the God who is above” web:Job.31.28), the verdict-formula עון פלילי that elsewhere at Job.31.11 closes one oath immediately preceding it (protasis Job.31.9, apodosis Job.31.10) rather than binding several protases together; the additive גַּם that opens Job.31.28 most directly continues from the astral material immediately before it (Job.31.26-Job.31.27) rather than reaching back to bind the wealth protases of Job.31.24-Job.31.25 into the same apodosis. That reading is disclosed as a live rival, not adopted: the row is chunked as written, with all three protases and the one following apodosis held inside its own span.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A plausible alternative treats wealth (Job.31.24-Job.31.25) and celestial worship (Job.31.26-Job.31.28) as two separate oaths, each with its own protasis clauses; the verdict-formula parallel with Job.31.11 (skeleton sweep of עון פלילי: 2 book-wide, Job.31.11 and Job.31.28) is disclosed as corroboration for reading Job.31.28's apodosis as answering the immediately preceding astral protasis specifically, rather than as one warrant spanning all three protases of this row, without redrawing the row's own frozen edges.
literature_type_guess: Oath against malicious joy when foes destroyed

boundary_rationale: Three further protases follow in sequence without a change of apodosis pattern: rejoicing at an enemy's ruin, אִם אֶ֭שְׂמַח בְּפִ֣יד מְשַׂנְאִ֑י ..., “If I have rejoiced at the destruction of him” (web:Job.31.29); a hospitality claim introduced by the 'if not' idiom, אִם לֹ֣א ..., at Job.31.31; and concealment of sin at Job.31.33, אִם כִּסִּ֣יתִי כְאָדָ֣ם פְּשָׁעָ֑י ..., “if like Adam I have covered my transgressions, by hiding my iniquity in my heart” (web:Job.31.33). The prefixed form כְאָדָ֣ם is anarthrous -- equally 'like a human being' and 'like Adam' on the bytes alone; the named-figure reading follows the WEB's own choice rather than an article-marked or otherwise disambiguated Hebrew form. The prefixed form itself is a genuine skeleton-tier singleton (sweep: 1 book-wide, Job.31.33); the bare lexeme אדם behind it sweeps 28 book-wide at skeleton tier and is not usable without disambiguation, since it also catches a same-consonant false positive inside this very row's own span at Job.31.34's וָ֝אֶדֹּ֗ם ('I kept silence', root D-M-M ('to be silent'), unrelated to אדם). The row closes on the fear-of-exposure statement at Job.31.34 ('so that I kept silence, and didn't go out of the door'), just before the broken-off appeal that opens Job.31.35.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The three topics (an enemy's downfall, hospitality, hidden sin) differ enough that three separate rows are defensible, but none of the intervening protasis clauses is answered by its own apodosis-curse the way the earlier oaths are, so the material is held together as one closing movement before the signature appeal.
literature_type_guess: Oath against stranger-deception and inhospitality fraud

boundary_rationale: The oath series breaks off for the signature plea: מִ֤י יִתֶּן לִ֨י שֹׁ֘מֵ֤עַֽ ..., “oh that I had one to hear me! Behold, here is my signature” (web:Job.31.35), a member of the two-word wish idiom מִ֤י יִתֶּן swept 9 verses book-wide at skeleton/consonantal tier (the pointed forms disagree across members: Job.11.5 reads יִתֵּ֣ן and Job.31.31 reads יִתֵּ֥ן, both against this verse's own יִתֶּן). Two of those nine are embedded, not the speaker's own wish: Job.31.31 sits inside a quoted household saying, and Job.11.5's יִתֵּ֣ן sits inside Zophar's speech (Job.11.1-Job.11.20, opened by וַ֭יַּעַן צֹפַ֥ר הַֽנַּעֲמָתִ֗י וַיֹּאמַֽר), not Job's -- the idiom is dialogue-wide, and both embedded members are disclosed here, not merely one of the two. Paseq falls in the OSHB seg layer at both Job.31.34 and Job.31.35 (oshb:Job.31.34 (paseq, single-witness); oshb:Job.31.35 (paseq, single-witness)), texture corroboration at the break. The protasis particle recurs once more inside this row at Job.31.36 (אִם לֹ֣א עַל ...), but here as an oath-affirmation idiom ('surely') answering the wish rather than opening a further self-curse, closing the row on Job.31.37's vow to approach God 'like a prince.'
strongest_rejected_alternative: Some would keep Job.31.35-Job.31.37 attached to the concealment oath just before it as its climax rather than a separate unit, but the wish-formula is a topic-turn interrogative-class marker distinct from every protasis clause around it, and no apodosis-curse connects Job.31.34 to what follows.
literature_type_guess: Wish-formula calling God to give written indictment

boundary_rationale: A final protasis returns after the signature plea: אִם עָ֭לַי אַדְמָתִ֣י תִזְעָ֑ק ..., “If my land cries out against me, and its furrows weep together;” (web:Job.31.38), the sixteenth of the chapter's 17-token protasis series (verse-initial skeleton sweep, Job.31.5 through Job.31.39). A second, coordinate land-stewardship protasis follows in the same row's own span at Job.31.39 (אִם כֹּ֭חָהּ אָכַ֣לְתִּי בְלִי כָ֑סֶף וְנֶ֖פֶשׁ בְּעָלֶ֣יהָ הִפָּֽחְתִּי, “if I have eaten its fruits without money, or have caused its owners to lose their life” web:Job.31.39) -- the series' true seventeenth and closing member, sharing Job.31.38's apodosis-curse at Job.31.40a (“let briers grow instead of wheat, and stinkweed instead of barley”) rather than opening one of its own. The narrator's colophon follows in the same verse, תַּ֝֗מּוּ דִּבְרֵ֥י אִיּֽוֹב, “The words of Job are ended.” (web:Job.31.40) -- a construction swept as a book-wide singleton (sweep: 1 book-wide) -- closing Job's speech before the narrator's prose resumes: “So these three men ceased to answer Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.” (web:Job.32.1). A petuchah follows Job.31.40 (oshb:Job.31.40 (petuchah, single-witness)), and the genre itself turns from verse to third-person prose at Job.32.1, doubling the colophon's own textual claim to end Job's words here.
strongest_rejected_alternative: This final protasis pair has sometimes been read as displaced from its rhetorical position after the Job.31.35-Job.31.37 signature plea; the argument against moving it rests on what the substrate actually carries -- the colophon at Job.31.40 and the petuchah following it (oshb:Job.31.40 (petuchah, single-witness)) fix the sequence in place as written -- rather than on a claim about a manuscript-variant apparatus not attested in this chapter (its ketiv/qere occurrences number 2 -- Job.31.11 and Job.31.20 -- neither inside Job.31.38-Job.31.40). The row chunks the Masoretic sequence as it stands rather than adopting a rearrangement.
literature_type_guess: Job's field-oath closing final defense with tears

boundary_rationale: The narrator closes out the three-cycle dialogue with a verdict rather than a fourth speech formula: “these three men ceased to answer Job” (web:Job.32.1), giving the reason with the closing clause כִּ֤י ה֖וּא צַדִּ֣יק בְּעֵינָֽיו – “he was righteous in his own eyes” (web:Job.32.1, oshb:Job.32.1). The sentence follows immediately on the colophon תַּ֝֗מּוּ דִּבְרֵ֥י אִיּֽוֹב "the words of Job are ended" (oshb:Job.31.40), a superscription/colophon-class boundary that belongs to the adjacent part; oshb:Job.32.1 (petuchah, single-witness) closes this verse on its own. The verse's grammatical subject, שְׁלֹ֤שֶׁת הָאֲנָשִׁ֣ים הָ֭אֵלֶּה “these three men,” settles the friends' role in the exchange before a new participant is named in the next verse, making this a self-contained narratorial beat rather than an opening clause of the Elihu introduction proper. The same two-word phrase closes the unit that follows, שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת הָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים (oshb:Job.32.5) — a byte-true bracket running from this row's own verse (32:1) to that row's closing verse (32:5) (skeleton sweep: 2 book-wide, sole members 32:1 and 32:5) that argues continuity across the seam at 32:1|32:2 as much as it argues separation. What keeps 32:1 as its own row is the participant shift (Elihu named with a genealogy from 32:2) together with the double petuchah (32:1 and 32:5, both single-witness), not the phrase by itself.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding this verse into the following Elihu-introduction row was considered and set aside, since its subject and verb belong to the friends' side of the account, not to Elihu's.
literature_type_guess: Three-friends' silence closing dialogue before Elihu

boundary_rationale: Elihu enters as a new participant with a genealogy inside the narrator's wrath notice: וַיִּ֤חַר אַ֨ף אֱלִיה֣וּא בֶן בַּרַכְאֵ֣ל הַבּוּזִי֮ מִמִּשְׁפַּ֪חַ֫ת רָ֥ם בְּ֭אִיּוֹב חָרָ֣ה אַפּ֑וֹ עַֽל צַדְּק֥וֹ נַ֝פְשׁ֗וֹ מֵאֱלֹהִֽים – WEB: “Then the wrath of Elihu the son of Barachel, the Buzite, of the family of Ram, was kindled against Job. His wrath was kindled because he justified himself rather than God.” (web:Job.32.2, oshb:Job.32.2). Naming the object first: the wrath-of-Elihu notice is not stated twice but sweep: 4 tokens over 3 verses — two inside 32:2 itself (against Job, then restated), a third against the friends at 32:3, וּבִשְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת רֵעָיו֮ חָרָ֪ה אַ֫פּ֥וֹ עַ֤ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא מָצְא֣וּ מַעֲנֶ֑ה וַ֝יַּרְשִׁ֗יעוּ אֶת אִיּֽוֹב – “Also his wrath was kindled against his three friends, because they had found no answer, and yet had condemned Job.” (web:Job.32.3, oshb:Job.32.3), and a fourth resuming the notice at the unit's close. The parenthetical on Elihu's deference to age, וֶֽאֱלִיה֗וּ חִכָּ֣ה אֶת אִ֭יּוֹב בִּדְבָרִ֑ים כִּ֤י זְֽקֵנִים הֵ֖מָּה מִמֶּ֣נּוּ לְיָמִֽים – “Now Elihu had waited to speak to Job, because they were older than he.” (web:Job.32.4, oshb:Job.32.4) – spells the name defectively (vav-aleph-lamed-yod-heh-vav, lacking the final aleph carried at 32:2 and resumed at 32:5) – sits inside that frame before the wrath-notice resumes and closes it: וַיַּ֤רְא אֱלִיה֗וּא כִּ֘י אֵ֤ין מַעֲנֶ֗ה בְּ֭פִי שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת הָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים וַיִּ֥חַר אַפּֽוֹ – “When Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouth of these three men, his wrath was kindled.” (web:Job.32.5, oshb:Job.32.5). oshb:Job.32.5 (petuchah, single-witness) closes this unit the same way oshb:Job.32.1 closed the one before it.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the wrath-against-Job clause (32:2-3) from the waiting-and-eruption clause (32:4-5) into two rows was considered and rejected, since the repeated wrath notice frames 32:4 as one continuous aside rather than two independent beats.
literature_type_guess: Elihu's wrathful prose introduction entering discourse

boundary_rationale: The speech formula opens the row, וַיַּ֤עַן אֱלִיה֖וּא בֶן בַּֽרַכְאֵ֥ל הַבּוּזִ֗י וַיֹּ֫אמַ֥ר (oshb:Job.32.6) – the tier-1 seam already fixed at the prose-to-poetry hinge – introducing Elihu's opening plea of youth against age, צָ֘עִ֤יר אֲנִ֣י לְ֭יָמִים וְאַתֶּ֣ם יְשִׁישִׁ֑ים: “I am young, and you are very old” (web:Job.32.6, oshb:Job.32.6). He recalls the premise he had deferred to, אָ֭מַרְתִּי יָמִ֣ים יְדַבֵּ֑רוּ – “I said, ‘Days should speak” (web:Job.32.7, oshb:Job.32.7), then overturns it with the adversative particle, אָ֭כֵן רֽוּחַ הִ֣יא בֶאֱנ֑וֹשׁ – “there is a spirit in man” (web:Job.32.8, oshb:Job.32.8), denying that age alone confers understanding (web:Job.32.9). The row closes when the same verb of thought returns transformed, לָכֵ֣ן אָ֭מַרְתִּי "Therefore I said" (oshb:Job.32.10), reversing 32:7's opening verb into a resolve to speak; the next row opens with a fresh presentative rather than continuing this frame.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Ending the row at 32:7, right after the deferred premise, was considered and set aside, since the adversative pivot at 32:8 and its echo-and-reversal at 32:10 complete one argumentative arc.
literature_type_guess: Elihu's exordium humble deference to elder wisdom

boundary_rationale: A presentative topic-turn opens the row, הֵ֤ן הוֹחַ֨לְתִּי לְֽדִבְרֵיכֶ֗ם – “Behold, I waited for your words” (web:Job.32.11, oshb:Job.32.11), addressing the friends in the second person as Elihu reviews their failure to convince Job (web:Job.32.12). He then warns them against claiming wisdom for themselves, פֶּן תֹּ֣֭אמְרוּ מָצָ֣אנוּ חָכְמָ֑ה – “Beware lest you say, ‘We have found wisdom” (web:Job.32.13, oshb:Job.32.13), and closes by distinguishing his own approach from theirs: Job's words were not directed against him, so he will not answer with their arguments (web:Job.32.14). The row ends before the address shifts from second-person "you" to a third-person description of the friends at 32:15.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row through 32:18 to keep the whole review-of-the-friends material together was considered and rejected, since 32:15 shifts from addressing the friends as "you" to describing them in the third person.
literature_type_guess: Elihu's reproach when friends find Job no rebuttal

boundary_rationale: The address pivots from second-person "you" to a third-person description of the friends' silence, חַ֭תּוּ לֹא עָ֣נוּ ע֑וֹד הֶעְתִּ֖יקוּ מֵהֶ֣ם מִלִּֽים – “"They are amazed. They answer no more. They don't have a word to say.” (web:Job.32.15, oshb:Job.32.15), and the same closing collocation recurs at the consonantal/skeleton tier (sweep: 2 book-wide, sole members 32:15 and 32:16; the pointing differs on both final words) at the end of the rhetorical question that follows, וְ֭הוֹחַלְתִּי כִּי לֹ֣א יְדַבֵּ֑רוּ כִּ֥י עָ֝מְד֗וּ לֹא עָ֥נוּ עֽוֹד – “Shall I wait, because they don't speak, because they stand still, and answer no more?” (web:Job.32.16, oshb:Job.32.16). Elihu then resolves to take his turn, אַעֲנֶ֣ה אַף אֲנִ֣י חֶלְקִ֑י אֲחַוֶּ֖ה דֵעִ֣י אַף אָֽנִי – “I also will answer my part, and I also will show my opinion.” (web:Job.32.17, oshb:Job.32.17), explaining the pressure behind it (web:Job.32.18) before the next row opens with a fresh presentative and a new image.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating the friends' silence and the wineskin-and-pledge material together as one eight-verse row was considered and rejected, since the presentative that opens 32:19 introduces a distinct image.
literature_type_guess: Elihu's spirit-compulsion urgency to break silence

boundary_rationale: A fresh presentative opens a new image, הִנֵּֽה בִטְנִ֗י כְּיַ֥יִן לֹא יִפָּתֵ֑חַ – “my breast is as wine which has no vent” (web:Job.32.19, oshb:Job.32.19), picking up the "I am full of words" pressure named the verse before (web:Job.32.18) and resolving it into the intent to speak (web:Job.32.20). The row then turns to a pledge of impartiality, אַל נָ֭א אֶשָּׂ֣א פְנֵי אִ֑ישׁ – “don't let me respect any man's person” (web:Job.32.21, oshb:Job.32.21), reasoned through to the chapter's close (web:Job.32.22). The row's end also lands on the chapter division, though that division carries no independent evidentiary weight; the row-boundary itself rests on the vocative naming of Job that opens the next row at 33:1.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Carrying this row across the chapter division into the address that follows was considered and rejected, since Elihu names Job directly there and turns the speech from self-description toward addressing him.
literature_type_guess: Elihu overflowing with words pressing toward utterance

boundary_rationale: Elihu turns to address Job by name: 33:1 opens the vocative naming of Job and shifts the addressee from the friends (plural, addressed across the preceding rows of this speech) to Job (singular), וְֽאוּלָ֗ם שְׁמַֽע נָ֣א אִיּ֣וֹב מִלָּ֑י וְֽכָל דְּבָרַ֥י הַאֲזִֽינָה – “"However, Job, please hear my speech, and listen to all my words.” (web:Job.33.1, oshb:Job.33.1), opening an invitation to a fair hearing that runs through the row: he has opened his mouth in sincerity (web:Job.33.2-33.3), claims the same creaturely origin as Job's Maker, הֵן אֲנִ֣י כְפִ֣יךָ לָאֵ֑ל מֵ֝חֹ֗מֶר קֹרַ֥צְתִּי גַם אָֽנִי – “Behold, I am toward God even as you are. I am also formed out of the clay.” (web:Job.33.6, oshb:Job.33.6). Its companion claim, the divine-spirit clause at 33:4, רֽוּחַ אֵ֥ל עָשָׂ֑תְנִי וְנִשְׁמַ֖ת שַׁדַּ֣י תְּחַיֵּֽנִי – “The Spirit of God has made me, and the breath of the Almighty gives me life.” (web:Job.33.4, oshb:Job.33.4), is pointed byte-identical in its core to 32:8's parallel clause (pointed byte sweep: 2 book-wide, sole members 32:8 and 33:4) — a byte-twinned formula binding Elihu's opening pivot to this address movement. Elihu issues a challenge, אִם תּוּכַ֥ל הֲשִׁיבֵ֑נִי עֶרְכָ֥ה לְ֝פָנַ֗י הִתְיַצָּֽבָה – “If you can, answer me. Set your words in order before me, and stand up.” (web:Job.33.5, oshb:Job.33.5), and reassures him of no terror (web:Job.33.7). The row closes before the discourse-quotation frame opens at 33:8.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating this row and the quoted material after it as one longer unit was considered and rejected, since the quotation frame at 33:8 marks a change of voice from Elihu's own address to a report of Job's words.
literature_type_guess: Elihu's appeal for Job's close attention to speaking

boundary_rationale: A 2ms perfect verb of speaking opens the row, אַ֭ךְ אָמַ֣רְתָּ בְאָזְנָ֑י וְק֖וֹל מִלִּ֣ין אֶשְׁמָֽע – “"Surely you have spoken in my hearing, I have heard the voice of your words, saying,” (web:Job.33.8, oshb:Job.33.8), introducing material voiced in 1cs at 33:9 that the speaker of 33:8 cannot be making about himself: זַ֥ךְ אֲנִ֗י בְּֽלִ֫י פָ֥שַׁע חַ֥ף אָנֹכִ֑י וְלֹ֖א עָוֺ֣ן לִֽי – “'I am clean, without disobedience. I am innocent, neither is there iniquity in me.” (web:Job.33.9, oshb:Job.33.9), the charge that God treats him as an adversary (web:Job.33.10), and the closing image, יָשֵׂ֣ם בַּסַּ֣ד רַגְלָ֑י יִ֝שְׁמֹ֗ר כָּל אָרְחֹתָֽי – “He puts my feet in the stocks. He marks all my paths.'” (web:Job.33.11, oshb:Job.33.11). 2ms address to Job resumes at the next row's opening, הֶן זֹ֣את לֹא צָדַ֣קְתָּ אֶעֱנֶ֑ךָּ כִּֽי יִרְבֶּ֥ה אֱ֝ל֗וֹהַ מֵאֱנֽוֹשׁ – “"Behold, I will answer you. In this you are not just, for God is greater than man.” (web:Job.33.12, oshb:Job.33.12), marking the return from the reported 1cs voice to Elihu's own 2ms address — the seam's actual driver, not the WEB apparatus quotation mark at 33:11.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding 33:8-11 into the surrounding address as mere illustration rather than a separate row was considered and rejected, since the discourse frame marks a distinct voice, not Elihu's own.
literature_type_guess: Elihu recites Job's complaint of innocence injustice

boundary_rationale: Elihu's own voice resumes with a presentative, הֶן זֹ֣את לֹא צָדַ֣קְתָּ אֶעֱנֶ֑ךָּ כִּֽי יִרְבֶּ֥ה אֱ֝ל֗וֹהַ מֵאֱנֽוֹשׁ – “"Behold, I will answer you. In this you are not just, for God is greater than man.” (web:Job.33.12, oshb:Job.33.12), a direct reply to the quoted words just closed at 33:11. He presses a rhetorical question, מַ֭דּוּעַ אֵלָ֣יו רִיב֑וֹתָ כִּ֥י כָל דְּ֝בָרָ֗יו לֹ֣א יַעֲנֶֽה – “Why do you strive against him, because he doesn't give account of any of his matters?” (web:Job.33.13, oshb:Job.33.13), then states the thesis the rest of the speech will illustrate, כִּֽי בְאַחַ֥ת יְדַבֶּר אֵ֑ל וּ֝בִשְׁתַּ֗יִם לֹ֣א יְשׁוּרֶֽנָּה – “For God speaks once, yes twice, though man pays no attention.” (web:Job.33.14, oshb:Job.33.14). This is a short row: it was kept separate from the dream-vision example that follows because 33:15 opens with its own scene-setting phrase rather than continuing the thesis statement, and separate from the quoted material before it because it answers a quotation rather than reporting one.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging this row with the dream-vision illustration that follows into one seven-verse strophe was considered and rejected in favor of the sharper scene-opening boundary that “In a dream, in a vision of the night” (web:Job.33.15) supplies at 33:15.
literature_type_guess: Elihu's counter God judges justly and rightly

boundary_rationale: A new scene opens the row, בַּחֲל֤וֹם חֶזְי֬וֹן לַ֗יְלָה – “In a dream, in a vision of the night” (web:Job.33.15, oshb:Job.33.15), the opening illustration of the thesis just stated at 33:14: in sleep, God opens the ear and warns (web:Job.33.16-33.17), and the row closes on the result, יַחְשֹׂ֣ךְ נַ֭פְשׁוֹ מִנִּי שָׁ֑חַת – “He keeps back his soul from the pit” (web:Job.33.18, oshb:Job.33.18). The next row opens a second illustration with a change of scene from dream to sickbed.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching this row to the argumentative material before it as one continuous unit was considered and rejected, since 33:15's dream-scene opening is a distinct topic-turn from the material that precedes it.
literature_type_guess: God's nocturnal instruction through visions dreams

boundary_rationale: A second illustration opens with a change of scene from dream to sickbed, וְהוּכַ֣ח בְּ֭מַכְאוֹב עַל מִשְׁכָּב֑וֹ וריב וְר֖וֹב עֲצָמָ֣יו אֵתָֽן – “"He is chastened also with pain on his bed, with continual strife in his bones,” (web:Job.33.19, oshb:Job.33.19; this verse carries a ketiv/qere note, single-witness), tracing the body's wasting through loss of appetite (web:Job.33.20) and flesh (web:Job.33.21; also a ketiv/qere verse, single-witness) to וַתִּקְרַ֣ב לַשַּׁ֣חַת נַפְשׁ֑וֹ וְ֝חַיָּת֗וֹ לַֽמְמִתִֽים – “Yes, his soul draws near to the pit, and his life to the destroyers.” (web:Job.33.22, oshb:Job.33.22); 'pit' recurs here at the skeleton tier (sweep: 7 book-wide: 9:31, 17:14, 33:18, 33:22, 33:24, 33:28, 33:30), not as an identical pointed form to 33:18's bare מֵעֲבֹ֥ר — 33:22 carries its own prefixed form נַפְשׁ֑וֹ. The next row opens a third illustration with its own protasis.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating this row as a continuation of the dream illustration before it was considered and rejected, since 33:19 opens a distinct affliction scene rather than extending the dream scene.
literature_type_guess: Sickness bringing nearness to death's appointed boundary

boundary_rationale: A third illustration opens on its own protasis, אִם יֵ֤שׁ עָלָ֨יו מַלְאָ֗ךְ מֵלִ֗יץ – “If there is beside him an angel, an interpreter” (web:Job.33.23, oshb:Job.33.23), answered by the apodosis of a quoted divine ransom, פְּ֭דָעֵהוּ מֵרֶ֥דֶת שָׁ֗חַת מָצָ֥אתִי כֹֽפֶר – “Deliver him from going down to the pit, I have found a ransom” (web:Job.33.24, oshb:Job.33.24). Restoration follows in flesh and prayer (web:Job.33.25-33.26), closing with a second quoted voice, the sufferer's own confession-song, ending “He has redeemed my soul from going into the pit. My life will see the light.’” (web:Job.33.28; this verse carries two ketiv/qere notes, single-witness). The next row opens with a fresh presentative summarizing the whole catalogue rather than continuing this scene.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row into the summary that follows to keep it attached to the scene it recaps was considered and rejected, since the presentative that opens the summary reads as a recap of all three illustrations, not an extension of the mediator scene alone.
literature_type_guess: Messenger-advocate interceding one against thousand deaths

boundary_rationale: A presentative opens a summary of the three illustrations, הֶן כָּל אֵ֭לֶּה יִפְעַל אֵ֑ל פַּעֲמַ֖יִם שָׁל֣וֹשׁ עִם גָּֽבֶר – “"Behold, God does all these things, twice, yes three times, with a man,” (web:Job.33.29, oshb:Job.33.29), echoing the thesis stated at 33:14, “For God speaks once, yes twice, though man pays no attention.” (web:Job.33.14, oshb:Job.33.14), with 33:29's own escalation to "twice, yes three times," and extending the "pit"/light language of the illustrations into a closing statement (web:Job.33.30). Elihu then addresses Job by name a second time in this speech, הַקְשֵׁ֖ב אִיּ֥וֹב שְֽׁמַֽע לִ֑י הַ֝חֲרֵ֗שׁ וְאָנֹכִ֥י אֲדַבֵּֽר – “Mark well, Job, and listen to me. Hold your peace, and I will speak.” (web:Job.33.31, oshb:Job.33.31), inviting a response (web:Job.33.32) before the speech closes, אִם אַ֭יִן אַתָּ֥ה שְֽׁמַֽע לִ֑י הַ֝חֲרֵ֗שׁ וַאֲאַלֶּפְךָ֥ חָכְמָֽה – “If not, listen to me. Hold your peace, and I will teach you wisdom."” (web:Job.33.33, oshb:Job.33.33). A setumah follows oshb:Job.33.33 (setumah, single-witness). The next speech opens at 34:1 with a fresh vaya'an formula, וַיַּ֥עַן אֱלִיה֗וּא וַיֹּאמַֽר — the tier-1 driver for the 33:33|34:1 seam: the formula and the mark both close this speech before the next one begins.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Ending the row at 33:30, keeping the summary with the mediator scene it recaps, was considered and rejected, since the vocative naming of Job at 33:31 reopens direct address and closes the speech on its own footing, paralleling the opening address at 33:1.
literature_type_guess: Elihu's closing exhortation for Job to hear wisdom

boundary_rationale: Elihu's second speech opens here with the verse-initial vaya'an formula, oshb:Job.34.1 “וַיַּ֥עַן אֱלִיה֗וּא וַיֹּאמַֽר”, carrying the full spelling אֱלִיה֗וּא (skeleton, byte-verified) rather than the defective אֱלִיה֗וּ that opens the next speech inside this same part at 35:1 — the two spellings are distinct members of the same speaker-token family, not interchangeable. The formula immediately launches a direct imperative address to a plural audience, web:Job.34.2 “"Hear my words, you wise men. Give ear to me, you who have knowledge.”, widened at web:Job.34.4 “Let us choose for us that which is right. Let us know among ourselves what is good.” into a joint invitation to judge together, closing the exordium before Elihu turns to a direct citation of Job's claim in the strophe that follows. The prior speech (Elihu's opening speech, formula-opened at 32:6) closes with a SAMEKH mark at oshb:Job.33.33 (samekh, single-witness), a mark that itself sits outside this speech's span, before the fresh vaya'an-formula address begins this second speech at 34:1.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 34:1 as a bare colophon line closing off Elihu's opening speech was rejected because the vaya'an formula is verse-initial and speech-opening throughout the book's dialogue spine, not speech-closing.
literature_type_guess: Elihu invites wise listeners into corporate judgment

boundary_rationale: A quotation frame opens this strophe, oshb:Job.34.5 “כִּֽי אָ֭מַר אִיּ֣וֹב צָדַ֑קְתִּי וְ֝אֵ֗ל הֵסִ֥יר מִשְׁפָּטִֽי”, citing Job by name here: web:Job.34.5 “For Job has said, ‘I am righteous, God has taken away my right.”. This marks a distinct move from the general address of the exordium above to naming Job's specific claim, sharpened by the comparison formula at oshb:Job.34.7 “מִי גֶ֥בֶר כְּאִיּ֑וֹב יִֽשְׁתֶּה לַּ֥עַג כַּמָּֽיִם” (“What man is like Job”, web:Job.34.7 “What man is like Job, who drinks scorn like water,”), and closed by a second quotation frame restating the profit-denial charge at 34:9. The strophe is bounded by two discourse-frame markers (כי אמר at 34:5 and again at 34:9) that both cite Job's supposed words rather than address the audience directly.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding this citation block into the exordium above was rejected because the quotation frame at 34:5 pivots from addressing an audience to naming and citing Job specifically, a discourse-frame shift rather than mere continuation.
literature_type_guess: Elihu quotes Job's injustice-complaint and returns question

boundary_rationale: לָכֵ֤ן opens a fresh vocative address, oshb:Job.34.10 “לָכֵ֤ן אַ֥נֲשֵׁ֥י לֵבָ֗ב שִׁמְע֫וּ לִ֥י חָלִ֖לָה לָאֵ֥ל מֵרֶ֗שַׁע וְשַׁדַּ֥י מֵעָֽוֶל”, web:Job.34.10 “"Therefore listen to me, you men of understanding: far be it from God, that he should do wickedness, from the Almighty, that he should commit iniquity.”, pivoting from the citation of Job's claim to a general theological axiom: God cannot act wickedly (34:10-12), followed by a rhetorical question about who could hold him accountable (34:13) and a hypothetical withdrawal of the life-breath that would return all flesh to dust (34:14-15). The address אַ֥נֲשֵׁ֥י לֵבָ֗ב (“men of understanding”) recurs at the skeleton/consonantal tier at 34:34 (sweep: 2 book-wide, sole members 34:10 and 34:34; the niqqud differs — hataf-patah under the nun at 34:10 against sheva at 34:34, so “verbatim” overstates the tier), a deliberate inclusio bracketing this strophe against the closing strophe of the speech — but with subject/addressee inversion: 34:10 is vocative, addressed by the 2mp imperative שִׁמְע֫וּ, while 34:34's אַנְשֵׁ֣י לֵ֭בָב is the grammatical subject of a 3mp yiqtol (יֹ֣אמְרוּ), not an address.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending the previous citation block through v.15 was rejected because לכן at 34:10 opens a new vocative address that turns from Job's specific claim to a general axiom about divine justice.
literature_type_guess: God's axiom sustaining justice incompatible with iniquity

boundary_rationale: A conditional address opens this strophe, oshb:Job.34.16 “וְאִם בִּ֥ינָה שִׁמְעָה זֹּ֑את הַ֝אֲזִ֗ינָה לְק֣וֹל מִלָּֽי”, web:Job.34.16 “"If now you have understanding, hear this. Listen to the voice of my words.”, distinct from the plain-imperative address at 34:10, and the content turns to a fresh topic-turn interrogative at oshb:Job.34.17 “הַאַ֬ף שׂוֹנֵ֣א מִשְׁפָּ֣ט יַחֲב֑וֹשׁ וְאִם צַדִּ֖יק כַּבִּ֣יר תַּרְשִֽׁיעַ”, web:Job.34.17 “Should even one who hates justice govern? Will you condemn him who is righteous and mighty,”. The strophe develops the claim that God shows no partiality to kings, nobles, princes, or the rich (34:18-19), closing with the sudden, handless death of the mighty (34:20).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 34:16 as a continuation of the v.10 axiom was rejected because ואם marks a new conditional address and the content turns to a fresh interrogative about impartial judgment of rulers rather than the general principle stated before it.
literature_type_guess: God indicts kings and nobles by sovereign divine scrutiny

boundary_rationale: A referent shift from named classes of rulers to universal humanity opens this movement at oshb:Job.34.21 “כִּי עֵ֭ינָיו עַל דַּרְכֵי אִ֑ישׁ וְֽכָל צְעָדָ֥יו יִרְאֶֽה”, web:Job.34.21 “"For his eyes are on the ways of a man. He sees all his goings.” — the verse-initial causal particle כִּי is not itself a seam-grade signal here (it opens 8 of 37 verses in ch.34 alone — 34:3, 34:5, 34:9, 34:11, 34:21, 34:23, 34:31, 34:37 — and 82 book-wide, skeleton-swept over consonantal_index.json), so the row rests its near edge on the shift in referent specificity (kings/princes/nobles/rich at 34:18-20 narrowing no further, then “a man” universally at 34:21) rather than on the particle. Universal moral oversight follows: no darkness hides evildoers (34:22), no formal summons is needed before God (34:23), the mighty are broken and replaced (34:24-26), because they turned from following him (34:27), so that the cry of the poor and afflicted reaches him and he hears it (34:28), and he alone grants or withholds quietness over nation and individual alike (34:29-30). The ten verses run as one continuous argument with no address shift or discourse-frame break until the fresh quotation frame at 34:31, which is why the span sits at the upper edge of the strophe guide rather than splitting at, say, the night language of 34:25.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting this unit at the night language of 34:25 was rejected because no vocative or discourse-frame marker interrupts the argument between 34:21's opening claim and 34:30's close; the whole section elaborates one continuous claim about God's unhidden oversight.
literature_type_guess: Divine oversight spanning rulers to universal human conduct

boundary_rationale: A hypothetical quotation frame opens this short strophe, oshb:Job.34.31 “כִּֽי אֶל אֵ֭ל הֶאָמַ֥ר נָשָׂ֗אתִי לֹ֣א אֶחְבֹּֽל”, web:Job.34.31 “"For has any said to God, 'I am guilty, but I will not offend any more.”, imagining words of repentance Job has not in fact spoken, and closing with a direct challenge to the audience: web:Job.34.33 “Shall his recompense be as you desire, that you refuse it? For you must choose, and not I. Therefore speak what you know.”. The three verses stay in this hypothetical, second-person mode addressed about repentance and choice, before 34:34 pivots back to “men of understanding,” now as the grammatical subject of a 3mp yiqtol (יֹ֣אמְרוּ) rather than repeating the vocative that opened the speech's central section at 34:10.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging this three-verse challenge into the closing verdict below was rejected because it stays in the hypothetical repentance-speech register, while 34:34 reopens with “men of understanding” — now the subject of a 3mp yiqtol, a bracket with subject/addressee inversion against the 2mp-imperative vocative at 34:10 — rather than continuing the hypothetical register.
literature_type_guess: Unmade repentance speech with direct choice challenge

boundary_rationale: אַנְשֵׁ֣י לֵ֭בָב recurs at the skeleton/consonantal tier, oshb:Job.34.34 “אַנְשֵׁ֣י לֵ֭בָב יֹ֣אמְרוּ לִ֑י וְגֶ֥בֶר חָ֝כָ֗ם שֹׁמֵ֥עַֽ לִֽי”, web:Job.34.34 “Men of understanding will tell me, yes, every wise man who hears me:” (sweep: 2 book-wide, sole members 34:10 and 34:34; the niqqud differs — hataf-patah at 34:10 against sheva at 34:34), echoing the exordium's address at 34:10 as its grammatical SUBJECT here (3mp yiqtol יֹ֣אמְרוּ) rather than repeating that verse's 2mp-imperative vocative — a bracket with subject/addressee inversion opening the speech's closing strophe as the counterpart to that earlier appeal. Naming Job directly recurs here too: bare אִ֭יּוֹב at 34:35 (the SECOND bare token in this chapter, after 34:5) and אִיּ֣וֹב at 34:36 (the THIRD), a distinct count object from the prefixed כְּאִיּ֑וֹב at 34:7 that stands between them, quoting the verdict “Job speaks without knowledge” (web:Job.34.35 “'Job speaks without knowledge. His words are without wisdom.'”) and wishing him tried to the end (web:Job.34.36 “I wish that Job were tried to the end, because of his answering like wicked men.”), closing with the charge that he adds rebellion to sin, web:Job.34.37 “For he adds rebellion to his sin. He claps his hands among us, and multiplies his words against God."”. A SAMEKH mark follows oshb:Job.34.37 (samekh, single-witness) in the WLC, corroborating (not driving) the speech's end at this point.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 34:34 as a continuation of the repentance challenge above was rejected because אנשי לבב echoes the exordium's address at 34:10, marking a deliberate return to the appeal-to-the-wise register that closes the speech.
literature_type_guess: Closing verdict renaming Job, inclusio bracket on wise men

boundary_rationale: Elihu's third speech opens with a second vaya'an formula, oshb:Job.35.1 “וַיַּ֥עַן אֱלִיה֗וּ וַיֹּאמַֽר”, whose skeleton is the defective אליהו (five consonants, byte-verified from consonantal_index.json) rather than the full אליהוא (six consonants) at 34:1 — the same formula family, a distinct spelling member; among the book's four Elihu formula-verses (32:6, 34:1, 35:1, 36:1) this defective spelling is attested at 1 of these 4 verses (35:1). The formula opens a fresh address, immediately putting direct second-person questions to Job that restate his claim, web:Job.35.2 “Do you think this to be your right, or do you say, ‘My righteousness is more than God’s,’”, and promising an answer: web:Job.35.4 “I will answer you, and your companions with you.”. This follows the SAMEKH-marked close of the second speech at oshb:Job.34.37 (samekh, single-witness); unlike that speech's exordium, which addressed 'the wise' about Job in the third person, this exordium addresses Job himself directly.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 35:1 as a bare resumption of speech 2's argument was rejected because the verse-initial vaya'an formula recurs here as it did at 34:1, marking a fresh speech-opening even though the spelling of Elihu's name differs.
literature_type_guess: Third speech exordium: direct address promise to answer Job

boundary_rationale: An imperative pair opens a fresh strophe, oshb:Job.35.5 “הַבֵּ֣ט שָׁמַ֣יִם וּרְאֵ֑ה וְשׁ֥וּר שְׁ֝חָקִ֗ים גָּבְה֥וּ מִמֶּֽךָּ”, web:Job.35.5 “Look to the skies, and see. See the skies, which are higher than you.”, pivoting from the promise to answer at 35:4 to a cosmic-transcendence argument developed through paired conditionals (35:6-8): sin or righteousness reaches one's fellow human beings, not God himself. The אם-clauses here are texture inside one strophe, not the extended protasis-apodosis series that structures the oath list of chapter 31.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding 35:5-8 into the exordium above was rejected because the imperative pair 'look... and see' opens a distinct cosmic-transcendence argument rather than continuing the direct promise-to-answer of 35:4.
literature_type_guess: Imperative cosmic-height argument: human conduct reaches humans only

boundary_rationale: A new topic opens with a participant shift from the second-person argument above to a third-person scenario, oshb:Job.35.9 “מֵ֭רֹב עֲשׁוּקִ֣ים יַזְעִ֑יקוּ יְשַׁוְּע֖וּ מִזְּר֣וֹעַ רַבִּֽים”, web:Job.35.9 “By reason of the multitude of oppressions they cry out. They cry for help by reason of the arm of the mighty.”: the oppressed cry out and go unanswered (35:9-10), despite being taught by the very order of creation (35:11), because of the pride of evil men (35:12), so that God will not hear an empty cry (35:13). The shift from 'you' (Job) to 'they' (the oppressed) marks the strophe's opening edge; the return to direct address at 35:14 marks its close.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 35:9-13 as a continuation of the transcendence argument's second-person address was rejected because these verses shift to third-person description of the oppressed before the direct application back to Job resumes at 35:14.
literature_type_guess: Third-person narrative of the oppressed cry unanswered

boundary_rationale: The 2ms verb תֹ֭אמַר reopens direct second-person address to Job, oshb:Job.35.14 “אַ֣ף כִּֽי תֹ֭אמַר לֹ֣א תְשׁוּרֶ֑נּוּ דִּ֥ין לְ֝פָנָ֗יו וּתְח֥וֹלֵֽל לֽוֹ”, web:Job.35.14 “How much less when you say you don't see him. The cause is before him, and you wait for him!”. The preceding אַ֣ף כִּֽי (skeleton sweep: 4 book-wide — 9:14, 15:16, 25:6, 35:14) is a dependent a-fortiori continuation of the clause before it in all four attested instances, not itself an independent opener; here it intensifies 35:13's אַךְ שָׁ֭וְא לֹא יִשְׁמַ֥ע אֵ֑ל וְ֝שַׁדַּ֗י לֹ֣א יְשׁוּרֶֽנָּה, and the same root crosses the row's own near seam (יְשׁוּרֶֽנָּה at 35:13 against תְשׁוּרֶ֑נּוּ at 35:14) as continuity texture disclosed here and argued against: the seam is carried instead by the shift back to direct 2ms address in תֹ֭אמַר, applying the transcendence argument specifically to Job's complaint that God does not see him. The speech, and this part, close at 35:16 with the prefixed token וְ֭אִיּוֹב, oshb:Job.35.16 “וְ֭אִיּוֹב הֶ֣בֶל יִפְצֶה פִּ֑יהוּ בִּבְלִי דַ֝֗עַת מִלִּ֥ין יַכְבִּֽר”, web:Job.35.16 “therefore Job opens his mouth with empty talk, and he multiplies words without knowledge."”. A PE mark follows oshb:Job.35.16 (petuchah, single-witness) in the WLC; the next verse, 36:1, reopens with the vayosef formula, “Elihu also continued, and said,” (web:Job.36.1), rather than the vaya'an formula that opened both 34:1 and 35:1 inside this part — a formula-family change, disclosed here as the argument for this part's far edge.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this strophe through 36:1 was rejected because 35:16 completes the verdict clause begun by the prefixed ואיוב token, and both the mark evidence (PE, single-witness) and the formula evidence (vayosef replacing vaya'an) fall on the far side of that boundary.
literature_type_guess: Verdict closing third speech: Job speaks empty without knowledge

boundary_rationale: Elihu's fourth and final movement opens on the verse-initial formula וַיֹּ֥סֶף אֱלִיה֗וּא וַיֹּאמַֽר (“Elihu also continued, and said,”, web:Job.36.1), built on the root vayosef (ויסף), NOT the vaya'an (ויען) that opens Elihu's earlier three speeches at 32:6, 34:1, and 35:1 -- the formula family itself changes here, marking Elihu RESUMING rather than a fresh interlocutor response, the same continuation-verb Job uses at 27:1 and 29:1. Verses 2-4 are Elihu's captatio: “Bear with me a little, and I will show you; for I still have something to say on God’s behalf.” (web:Job.36.2), asking for patience before claiming his knowledge comes from afar, and closing on direct second-person address, תְּמִ֖ים דֵּע֣וֹת עִמָּֽךְ (‘perfect in knowledge is with you’, web:Job.36.4) -- the 2ms suffix on עמך (‘with you’) singles out Job as addressee before the doctrinal material begins at verse 5. The strophe is bounded at its close by the next presentative הן-opening at 36:5.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding 36:1 into the prior speech as a mere continuation verse was rejected because the vayosef formula still marks a fresh verse-initial discourse opening, the pattern this book treats as a seam everywhere else it occurs (27:1, 29:1).
literature_type_guess: Fourth speech captatio: Elihu resumes with patience request

boundary_rationale: A new movement opens on the presentative particle הֶן (“behold”): “"Behold, God is mighty, and doesn't despise anyone. He is mighty in strength of understanding.” (web:Job.36.5). The unit develops in three self-contained conditional sentences keyed to the particle אִֽם/וְאִם (“if”): וְאִם אֲסוּרִ֥ים בַּזִּקִּ֑ים יִ֝לָּכְד֗וּן בְּחַבְלֵי עֹֽנִי (“If they are bound in fetters, and are taken in the cords of afflictions,”, web:Job.36.8) opens a protasis answered within the wayyiqtol of the next verse, וַיַּגֵּ֣ד לָהֶ֣ם פָּעֳלָ֑ם וּ֝פִשְׁעֵיהֶ֗ם כִּ֣י יִתְגַּבָּֽרוּ (“then he shows them their work, and their transgressions, that they have behaved themselves proudly.”, web:Job.36.9); a second, independent conditional states the positive case within its own verse, אִֽם יִשְׁמְע֗וּ וְֽיַ֫עֲבֹ֥דוּ יְכַלּ֣וּ יְמֵיהֶ֣ם בַּטּ֑וֹב וּ֝שְׁנֵיהֶ֗ם בַּנְּעִימִֽים – “If they listen and serve him, they will spend their days in prosperity, and their years in pleasures.” (web:Job.36.11, oshb:Job.36.11); a third, likewise self-contained, states the negative case within its own verse, וְאִם לֹ֣א יִ֭שְׁמְעוּ בְּשֶׁ֣לַח יַעֲבֹ֑רוּ וְ֝יִגְוְע֗וּ כִּבְלִי דָֽעַת – “But if they don't listen, they will perish by the sword; they will die without knowledge.” (web:Job.36.12, oshb:Job.36.12) — obedient hearers prosper, the deaf perish without knowledge. The span closes on a verbal inclusio: 36:10 opens the ear (וַיִּ֣גֶל אָ֭זְנָם, the root גלה — ‘opens’ — plus its object אזן, ‘their ear’) and 36:15 closes on the same root-plus-object pairing at the skeleton tier (וְיִ֖גֶל בַּלַּ֣חַץ אָזְנָֽם, “opens their ear in oppression” in web:Job.36.15; 36:10’s verb carries a dagesh in the yod with its object accented dehi, while 36:15’s verb has no dagesh and its object carries a meteg instead, so identity holds at skeleton, not byte, tier) — the root גלה governing אזן brackets the whole unit before the address shifts from describing “them” to addressing “you” at 36:16.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting this span at the internal protasis in 36:8 was considered and set aside, since the addressee stays third-person throughout 5-15 and turns to direct 'you' at 36:16 instead, so the stronger participant-level seam sits there.
literature_type_guess: Three conditional scenarios: bound receive knowledge, obedient prosper

boundary_rationale: The address shifts from third-person description to direct second-person warning inside 36:16 itself: וְאַ֤ף הֲסִיתְךָ֨ (‘and also he has allured YOU’) carries a 2ms object suffix, WEB “Yes, he would have allured you out of distress, into a wide place, where there is no restriction. That which is set on your table would be full of fatness.” (web:Job.36.16). The pivot continues explicitly in the next verse's opening, “But you are full of the judgment of the wicked. Judgment and justice take hold of you.” (web:Job.36.17). The unit is a sustained warning against wrath, bribery, and desiring 'the night' (36:20), closing on the admonition “Take heed, don’t regard iniquity; for you have chosen this rather than affliction.” (web:Job.36.21) before the discourse returns to third-person praise of God on the next presentative הן at 36:22.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Anchoring the seam one verse later at 36:16|36:17, so the strophe would open at Job.36.17’s own 2ms-perfect verb מָלֵ֑אתָ (web:Job.36.17, oshb:Job.36.17), was considered and rejected, since the 2ms object suffix already lands on 36:16's own second word (הֲסִיתְךָ֨, “allured you” in web:Job.36.16), with no third-person clause preceding it inside that verse to narrate through; the address shift is therefore already underway at 36:16, not withheld until 36:17.
literature_type_guess: Warning pivot to Job as you: against wrath and desire

boundary_rationale: A fresh presentative הֶן-opening returns the discourse to third-person praise: “Behold, God is exalted in his power. Who is a teacher like him?” (web:Job.36.22), followed by the paired rhetorical questions of 36:23, “Who has prescribed his way for him? Or who can say, ‘You have committed unrighteousness’?” (web:Job.36.23), asking who may prescribe God's way or charge him with wrong. The unit closes with an imperative pivot, “Remember that you magnify his work, about which men have sung.” (web:Job.36.24), and a universal-viewing statement at 36:25 before the next הן-opening at 36:26 begins a new movement on the same root theme of divine greatness.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Running 22-29 together as one hen-to-hen span was considered, but 36:26 opens its own self-contained water-cycle unit closed by its own question at 36:29, so the two hen-strophes are kept separate.
literature_type_guess: Presentative praise with rhetorical questions about prescribing God

boundary_rationale: A third הֶן-opening begins the unit: “Behold, God is great, and we don't know him. The number of his years is unsearchable.” (web:Job.36.26), stating וְלֹ֣א נֵדָ֑ע (“we don't know him” at web:Job.36.26). Verses 27-28 describe the water cycle — rain drawn up and poured down — and the strophe closes on a matching cognitive verb from a different root, אַ֣ף אִם יָ֭בִין מִפְרְשֵׂי עָ֑ב תְּ֝שֻׁא֗וֹת סֻכָּתֽוֹ (“Indeed, can anyone understand the spreading of the clouds and the thunderings of his pavilion?”, web:Job.36.29). The bracket is thematic rather than a shared lexical root — the opening colon’s closing verb וְלֹ֣א נֵדָ֑ע (“know”) and the verse’s closing verb (“understand”) come from two different roots — but both frame the same claim that the meteorological mechanism is beyond human grasp. The same opening-colon collocation וְלֹ֣א נֵדָ֑ע recurs in verse-final position at the skeleton tier at 37:5’s וְלֹ֣א נֵדָֽע (differing only in final accent; skeleton sweep: 4 book-wide — 8:9, 15:9, 36:26, 37:5), a skeleton-tier bracket straddling both this row’s own far seam (36:29|36:30) and the downstream 37:1|37:2 seam; disclosed here as continuity texture weighed against the strophe division rather than as a boundary override, since Elihu's fourth speech (36:1-37:24) is one continuous unit regardless of where its rows are cut. The unit closes before a fourth הֶן-opening — at the combined/skeleton tier (segol הֶן at 36:5/36:22/36:26 plus tsere הֵן at 36:30, sweep: 4 verse-initial occurrences in ch.36) — turns to lightning at 36:30.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 'we do not know' and 'can he understand' as one lexical inclusio was avoided on purpose, since the two verbs come from different roots (ידע and בין); the bracket is argued as thematic, not as root repetition.
literature_type_guess: Water cycle cosmology: divine mechanism beyond human knowing grasp

boundary_rationale: “Behold, he spreads his light around him. He covers the bottom of the sea.” (web:Job.36.30) opens on the FOURTH הֵן within this chapter at the combined skeleton tier (segol הֶן sweep: 10 book-wide/9 verse-initial, with ch.36 members 36:5/36:22/36:26; accent-free tsere הֵן sweep: 4 verse-initial book-wide — 27:12, 33:6, 36:30, MT 41:1 — with a further 17 verse-initial tokens carrying cantillation as a separate accent-bearing sub-object; folding the segol and accent-free-tsere sub-objects into one skeleton-tier count of 4 verse-initial occurrences in ch.36 gives the ordinal “fourth”), describing lightning and the storm as the agents of judgment: “For by these he judges the people. He gives food in abundance.” (web:Job.36.31). The unit runs through the storm's noise at 36:33 and crosses the chapter number — a tier-4 boundary, not itself evidentiary — into 37:1, where the deictic אַף לְ֭זֹאת (“Yes, at this” in web:Job.37.1) ties Elihu's own bodily tremor back to the storm just narrated, closing the strophe on Elihu's own reaction rather than opening a new one. The next verse's plural imperative (שִׁמְע֤וּ שָׁמ֣וֹעַ, “hear, oh hear”) launches a fresh, audience-directed unit.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Starting the next row at 37:1 rather than 37:2 was considered, since a new chapter number sits there, but the chapter break is tier-4 and the deictic 'at this' in 37:1 grammatically closes the storm description rather than opening the imperative section that follows.
literature_type_guess: Lightning as judgment agent, moving from description to Elihu tremor

boundary_rationale: A plural imperative opens the unit: “Hear, oh, hear the noise of his voice, the sound that goes out of his mouth.” (web:Job.37.2), the verb שִׁמְע֤וּ שָׁמ֣וֹעַ (‘hear, oh hear’) built on an infinitive-absolute intensifier and addressed to listeners rather than to God or Job by name -- a discourse-frame shift distinct from both the hymn's הן-openings before it and the direct 'you'-address after it. The unit describes the thunder's roar through 37:4-5, closing on “God thunders marvelously with his voice. He does great things, which we can’t comprehend.” (web:Job.37.5), before the causal כִּ֤י (‘for’) opens a quotation frame at 37:6.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping 37:1-5 together as one span was set aside because 37:1 is Elihu's own bodily response closing the prior unit, while 37:2's plural imperative opens a distinct audience-directed call to attention.
literature_type_guess: Call-to-attention imperative on thunder and divine voice

boundary_rationale: A shift to divine speech-content addressed to the elements opens the unit: כִּ֤י לַשֶּׁ֨לַג יֹאמַ֗ר הֱוֵ֫א אָ֥רֶץ וְגֶ֥שֶׁם מָטָ֑ר וְ֝גֶ֗שֶׁם מִטְר֥וֹת עֻזּֽוֹ – “For he says to the snow, 'Fall on the earth,' likewise to the shower of rain, and to the showers of his mighty rain.” (web:Job.37.6, oshb:Job.37.6) — the quoted imperative content (snow and rain commanded to fall) marks a fresh topic distinct from 37:5's close on thunder generally; the verse-initial particle כִּ֤י itself is a subordinating causal, not a member of the discourse-opener family (the book's verse-initial speech-formula inventory for chapters 32-40 lists 8 members — 32:6, 34:1, 35:1, 36:1, 38:1, 40:1, 40:3, 40:6 — none at 37:6), so the seam rests on the addressee/content shift to the elements rather than on any kinship with the wisdom poem's frame-vayomer climax verse. The material moves through ice and the north wind (37:9-10) to clouds turned by his guidance, “It is turned around by his guidance, that they may do whatever he commands them on the surface of the habitable world,” (web:Job.37.12), and closes on a threefold אִם clause, “whether it is for correction, or for his land, or for loving kindness, that he causes it to come.” (web:Job.37.13) — distinct from the self-imprecatory אִם-series of chapter 31 in function (here disjunctive “whether” rather than conditional oath), but the same particle closing a unit in a triad. Verse 37:12 carries a ketiv/qere pair, disclosed here since the quoted span crosses it (oshb:Job.37.12, ketiv/qere).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the ice material (6-10) from the cloud-guidance material (11-13) into two rows was tried but abandoned, since neither half carries its own discourse-frame marker independent of the quotation frame opening the whole unit at 37:6.
literature_type_guess: Divine commands to snow, rain, ice: quoted speech to elements

boundary_rationale: Elihu names Job directly, opening a fresh unit: הַאֲזִ֣ינָה זֹּ֣את אִיּ֑וֹב (‘listen to this, Job’, web:Job.37.14), WEB “Listen to this, Job. Stand still,” (web:Job.37.14). Within this speech's 57 verses, איוב (‘Job’) appears only here (sweep: 1 occurrence across Job.36.1-Job.37.24), matching the book-wide pattern in which Elihu, alone among the interlocutors, addresses Job by name inside speech. An anaphoric refrain follows -- הֲ֭תֵדַע at 37:15 and the byte-identical הֲ֭תֵדַע at 37:16 (‘do you know’, web:Job.37.15-Job.37.16) -- driving a series of rhetorical questions through 37:19-20 that closes on “Will it be told him that I would speak? Or should a man wish that he were swallowed up?” (web:Job.37.20) before the discourse returns to third-person description at 37:21.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this unit through 37:24 to the speech's end was considered, but 37:21 drops the second-person interrogatives and returns to third-person description, so the interrogative block is kept as its own span.
literature_type_guess: Direct naming of Job with anaphoric interrogative volley throughout

boundary_rationale: Third-person description resumes without an interrogative or vocative: “Now men don’t see the light which is bright in the skies, but the wind passes, and clears them.” (web:Job.37.21), moving through the golden splendor from the north (37:22) and the Almighty's inaccessibility (37:23) to the speech's closing line, “Therefore men revere him. He doesn’t regard any who are wise of heart.” (web:Job.37.24). A PE mark follows this verse in the Masoretic tradition (oshb:Job.37.24, petuchah, single-witness) -- tier-3 corroboration that sits exactly at this part's closing seam. What follows at 38:1 is a full participant and register change: a fresh vaya'an formula, וַיַּֽעַן יְהוָ֣ה (‘and he answered, Yahweh’, web:Job.38.1), opening the earliest of the three YHWH vaya'an formulas in the book (sweep: 3 book-wide, at 38:1/40:1/40:6) and the Tetragrammaton's initial speech, carrying the ketiv/qere pair מנ הסערה (ketiv) / מִ֥ן הַסְּעָרָ֗ה (qere) inside the formula (‘out of the whirlwind’) -- disclosed here since the seam argument cites it. Chapter 38 itself carries no Masoretic paragraph mark of its own, so from this side the 38:1 seam rests on the formula and the speaker change alone, with the 37:24 mark noted above as weak corroboration alongside it.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Carrying this span through 38:1 as one continuous unit was rejected outright, since 38:1 introduces an entirely new speaker, Yahweh, on its own verse-initial formula -- a participant change, not a continuation.
literature_type_guess: Third-person closure: men revere him, speech ends with PE mark

boundary_rationale: The narrative formula “Then Yahweh answered Job out of the whirlwind,” (web:Job.38.1) is the FIRST (sweep: 3 book-wide) of exactly three יְהוָ֣ה-spoken vaya'an tokens in the book, byte-settled in canonical verse order as 38:1, 40:1, 40:6, and it alone carries this part's opening seam against the close of Elihu's fourth speech at 37:24: chapter 38 carries none of the book's 39 Masoretic paragraph marks, so the seam rests on the formula. A petuchah (single-witness) does follow oshb:Job.37.24 — “Therefore men revere him. He doesn't regard any who are wise of heart."” (web:Job.37.24) — on the far side, closing Elihu's speech, but that corroboration belongs to the seam's other edge, not to chapter 38 itself. Inside the formula the ketiv מנ הסערה gives way to the qere מִ֥ן הַסְּעָרָ֗ה 'from the storm' (oshb:Job.38.1), and one paseq (single-witness) segments the verse. Verse 2 opens the direct address with the interrogative מִ֤י זֶ֨ה, “"Who is this who darkens counsel by words without knowledge?” (web:Job.38.2 — the phrase mi-zeh recurs once more only, at 42:3 (sweep: 2 book-wide), where Job quotes it back at his retraction, framing an inclusio across the whole interchange), carrying its own paseq (single-witness). Verse 3 opens with the imperative אֱזָר נָ֣א, “gird now,” followed by the gird-up device’s two-word counting core — the comparative כְגֶ֣בֶר (‘like a man’) plus the direct object חֲלָצֶ֑יךָ (‘your loins’) (sweep: 2 book-wide, sole members 38:3 and 40:7): אֱזָר נָ֣א כְגֶ֣בֶר חֲלָצֶ֑יךָ וְ֝אֶשְׁאָלְךָ֗ וְהוֹדִיעֵֽנִי – “Brace yourself like a man, for I will question you, then you answer me!” (web:Job.38.3, oshb:Job.38.3), the two-word phrase recurring at 40:7 and nowhere else (sweep: 2 book-wide), opening the second whirlwind speech in an identical parallel gesture.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the frame formula into its own one-verse row was set aside because 38:1's vaya'an and the 2-3 challenge form one uninterrupted address opening the interrogation, not two separable movements.
literature_type_guess: Yahweh first vaya'an: who darkens counsel, gird up challenge

boundary_rationale: The cosmos catalog's opening item begins with the interrogative אֵיפֹ֣ה הָ֭יִיתָ, “"Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth? Declare, if you have understanding.” (web:Job.38.4), matched by the chained מִי-questions at verses 5-6 (who determined the earth's measures, who stretched the line, who laid the cornerstone) and closing on the doxological image “when the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy?” (web:Job.38.7) — בְּנֵ֥י אֱלֹהִֽים “sons of God” (oshb:Job.38.7) casts creation as a scene the divine court witnessed — an echo, not a verbatim recurrence, of the frame's own court-language register: the frame's phrase is articled, בְּנֵ֣י הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים (skeleton sweep: 2 book-wide, sole members 1:6 and 2:1), while 38:7's is anarthrous, בְּנֵ֥י אֱלֹהִֽים (skeleton sweep: 1 book-wide, 38:7 only) — two distinct string objects bearing the same register. The item ends here because verse 8 turns to a new participant, the sea, rather than repeating the earth's-foundation questions.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A four-verse split at 5|6, isolating the cornerstone image on its own, was rejected: 38:5-6 carry the pronoun-מִי chain (מִי שָׂ֣ם/א֤וֹ מִֽי at 38:5, with 38:6's opening interrogative עַל מָ֭ה (“upon what”) a variant form rather than a break, and 38:6's own מִֽי closing the pair), and 38:7 is a dependent doxological close — not a fourth question — rather than a claim that all three verses run as one uninterrupted chain.
literature_type_guess: Foundations interrogative with morning stars and divine court scene

boundary_rationale: The sea item turns to a new participant without opening on a fresh interrogative pronoun: וַיָּ֣סֶךְ, “Or who shut up the sea with doors, when it broke out of the womb,” (web:Job.38.8, oshb:Job.38.8) — 3ms, still carrying the questioning force of the מִי that opened verses 5-6 by ellipsis, but marking the turn by subject-shift alone: from earth's foundations to the sea. Yahweh's own 1cs voice does not begin until the following verse, בְּשׂוּמִ֣י עָנָ֣ן לְבֻשׁ֑וֹ וַ֝עֲרָפֶ֗ל חֲתֻלָּתֽוֹ, “when I made clouds its garment, and wrapped it in thick darkness,” (web:Job.38.9, oshb:Job.38.9); the participant/topic shift at 38:8 is this item's own opening signal, and the 1cs voice at 38:9 is corroborating texture one verse inside the item, not the driver of the seam itself. The item closes with Yahweh's quoted command to the sea, “and said, 'You may come here, but no further. Your proud waves shall be stopped here'?” (web:Job.38.11), before verse 12 reopens with a fresh הְֽ֭מִיָּמֶיךָ-interrogative on a new topic, the dawn.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding the sea item into the foundations item above was set aside because the participant changes and the voice shifts away from bare address toward Yahweh speaking in his own voice, a break sharper than the shared questioning force by itself would suggest.
