literature_type_guess: Sea participant-shift: doors shut, Yahweh commands waves restrained

boundary_rationale: A fresh הֲ-interrogative opens the dawn item: הְֽ֭מִיָּמֶיךָ צִוִּ֣יתָ בֹּ֑קֶר, “Have you commanded the morning in your days, and caused the dawn to know its place,” (web:Job.38.12), with a K/Q pair inside the same verse — ketiv ידעתה שחר against qere יִדַּ֖עְתָּה הַשַּׁ֣חַר, WEB's gloss 'caused the dawn to know its place' (web:Job.38.12). The item carries the book's two suspended letters (sweep: 2 book-wide) in full: the seg עִ֣ suspended within רְשָׁעִ֣ים, WEB's 'the wicked,' as dawn shakes them 'out of it' (web:Job.38.13; oshb:Job.38.13 suspended ayin, single-witness), and again within מֵרְשָׁעִ֣ים at “From the wicked, their light is withheld. The high arm is broken.” (web:Job.38.15; oshb:Job.38.15 suspended ayin, single-witness). The item closes there before verse 16 opens a fresh הֲ֭בָאתָ question on the sea's depths.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this item through verse 18's earth-breadth question was rejected because 38:16 restarts with its own הֲ֭בָאתָ formula, matched verbatim at 38:22, marking a new movement.
literature_type_guess: Dawn interrogative with ketiv-qere and wicked shaken imagery

boundary_rationale: Two paired items share a row here. הֲ֭בָאתָ עַד נִבְכֵי יָ֑ם, “Have you entered into the springs of the sea? Or have you walked in the recesses of the deep?” (web:Job.38.16), opens the boundaries-of-earth item (16-18), closing with “Have you comprehended the earth in its width? Declare, if you know it all.” (web:Job.38.18). Verse 19 turns to a second interrogative device, the interrogative-adverb-plus-demonstrative construction אֵי זֶ֣ה הַ֭דֶּרֶךְ יִשְׁכָּן, “What is the way to the dwelling of light? As for darkness, where is its place,” (web:Job.38.19) — the identical phrase recurs once more only, at 38:24 (sweep: 2 book-wide), framing a light-motif that spans the row's far side. The pairing closes on the taunt “Surely you know, for you were born then, and the number of your days is great!” (web:Job.38.21) before verse 22 reopens with the same הֲ֭בָאתָ that opened this row. That verbatim repetition — not the mere presence of an interrogative-he opener, which recurs fifteen times across 38:16-39:12 — is what marks the next movement; this row's own unity across its two items rests on the shared theme, the limits of the knowable earth, argued below.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting this row at 18|19 into two three-verse rows was set aside because both items share one theme, the limits of the knowable earth, and the second closes with a taunt that answers the boundaries-of-earth question.
literature_type_guess: Earth boundaries and light-darkness dwelling with paired interrogatives

boundary_rationale: The precipitation cluster opens by repeating verbatim the formula that opened the row above: הֲ֭בָאתָ אֶל אֹצְר֣וֹת שָׁ֑לֶג, “Have you entered the storehouses of the snow, or have you seen the storehouses of the hail,” (web:Job.38.22). Its own near edge sits at the participant/topic shift from the light-and-darkness dwelling-place of the row before this one to snow-and-hail storehouses here; the fresh הֲ-interrogative opener is texture (fifteen such openers fall across 38:16-39:12) rather than the discriminator by itself. Interior turns follow at every new form water takes: אֵי זֶ֣ה הַ֭דֶּרֶךְ יֵחָ֣לֶק, “By what way is the lightning distributed, or the east wind scattered on the earth?” (web:Job.38.24) — the same interrogative-adverb-plus-demonstrative device that opened the row before this one at 38:19 (sweep: 2 book-wide, its only two members), recurring here mid-cluster rather than at an edge, disclosed rather than denied; its own two subjects, light and the east wind, are an outlier inside this otherwise water-forms cluster, not a further form of water. מִֽי פִלַּ֣ג לַשֶּׁ֣טֶף תְּעָלָ֑ה, “Who has cut a channel for the flood water, or the path for the thunderstorm,” (web:Job.38.25) turns to the flood channel on a fresh verse-initial bare מי, a member the interior-turn list must include alongside הֲיֵשׁ לַמָּטָ֥ר אָ֑ב, “Does the rain have a father? Or who fathers the drops of dew?” (web:Job.38.28), and מִבֶּ֣טֶן מִ֭י יָצָ֣א הַקָּ֑רַח, “Whose womb did the ice come out of? Who has given birth to the gray frost of the sky?” (web:Job.38.29), where the same pronoun sits as the verse's second word rather than its opener. The cluster closes on ice and the frozen deep, “The waters become hard like stone, when the surface of the deep is frozen.” (web:Job.38.30), before verse 31 turns to the constellations with its own fresh הֲ-interrogative.

boundary_rationale: This row closes the cosmos catalog across two interior turns. הַֽ֭תְקַשֵּׁר מַעֲדַנּ֣וֹת כִּימָ֑ה, “Can you bind the cluster of the Pleiades, or loosen the cords of Orion?” (web:Job.38.31), opens the constellations item on a patah-plus-meteg interrogative-he (not the more common hataf-patah spelling; the same patah-plus-meteg spelling recurs only at its sibling verse inside this row, 38:35 — sweep: 2 within the 38:16-39:12 catalog window; book-wide the spelling occurs in 9 verses (8 interrogative)), running through the heavens' laws at verse 33 (“Do you know the laws of the heavens? The description turns at verse 17 to a theological aside, כִּֽי הִשָּׁ֣הּ אֱל֣וֹהַּ, “because God has deprived her of wisdom, neither has he imparted to her understanding.” (web:Job.39.17), explaining the carelessness just described, before closing on the ostrich outrunning horse and rider (“When she lifts up herself on high, she scorns the horse and his rider.”, web:Job.39.18). boundary_rationale: הֲתִתֵּ֣ן לַסּ֣וּס גְּבוּרָ֑ה הֲתַלְבִּ֖ישׁ צַוָּאר֣וֹ רַעְמָֽה, “Have you given the horse might?
